Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

This replaces the band-around-wrists stability drill. Goodin's university CV identifies a PhD in Sport Physiology and Performance; this does not establish an individual exercise prescription.

entries.name: Band Lateral Raise
entries.editorialNote: Named exercise reference; compare the linked source setup with the internal technique notes.

entries.name: Band Triceps Pushdown
entries.editorialNote: Physitrack instructions specify a band secured above the head, upper arms beside the body and elbow extension downward. Sampled frames establish the standing high-anchor elastic-resistance setup. Upper-arm positioning and the complete elbow path need full-motion comparison before technique approval.

entries.name: Band Biceps Curl
entries.editorialNote: Written section confirms elbow flexion against a band anchored under the foot.

entries.name: Band Pallof Press
entries.editorialNote: Rehab Hero’s Pallof page explicitly describes an elastic band anchored to the side, hands starting at the chest and a forward press while resisting turn. Its original video previews show the standing band version, replacing PureGym’s cable demonstration. The source suggests longer holds than the catalog two-second pause. Hold duration remains a programming difference; the equipment and anti-rotation configuration are supported. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Band Woodchop
entries.editorialNote: Physitrack instructions and sampled frames show a standing high-anchored resistance band held in both hands and a diagonal pull toward the opposite hip. This replaces the cable-only comparison. Full video motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Mini-Band Lateral Walk
entries.editorialNote: NASM lateral band walk; band around ankles in the description. Compare with any above-knee placement.

entries.name: Mini-Band Monster Walk
entries.editorialNote: Forward band walk in an athletic stance, per written section.

entries.name: Banded Clamshell
entries.editorialNote: Written section confirms side-lying, bent knees, heels together and top-knee opening. Reverse-clamshell clip rejected.

entries.name: Banded Glute Bridge
entries.editorialNote: Named exercise reference; compare the linked source setup with the internal technique notes.

entries.name: Band Pull-Through
entries.editorialNote: Band anchored behind the hips; written section checked.

entries.name: Band Good Morning
entries.editorialNote: Named exercise reference; compare the linked source setup with the internal technique notes.

entries.name: Prone Band Hamstring Curl
entries.editorialNote: Rehab Hero explicitly describes a band secured low to a stable fixture, prone support and knee flexion while the other leg remains still. Public previews show that anchored prone curl. This replaces the loop-around-the-other-foot comparator. Band/cuff security still follows the product design.

entries.name: Battle Rope Alternating Waves
entries.editorialNote: Standing alternating rope-wave reference; amplitude remains adjustable.

entries.name: Battle Rope Side-to-Side Waves
entries.editorialNote: PluriMetrics and Austin Van Buskirk have original side-to-side-wave candidates whose previews show horizontal rope travel. Onnit’s current in-and-out waves instead separate and reunite the hands. Need hands moving together across the torso with the intended trunk turn, plus stronger documented professional provenance for the closer candidates. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Battle Rope Rotational Slams
entries.editorialNote: The BENSUEKTRAINING previews show a large rope arc, while Muscle & Strength’s current power-slam reference is a bilateral central slam. A credible source must establish an overhead-to-one-side slam with alternating sides; a central power slam does not demonstrate the rotational sequence. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Battle Rope Double Slams
entries.editorialNote: Onnit original Power Slam public previews show both battle-rope ends raised together and driven toward the floor from a standing stance. This establishes the simultaneous double slam rather than alternating waves. No rotational phase or lateral travel is implied.

entries.name: Battle Rope Lateral Shuffle Waves
entries.editorialNote: PluriMetrics’ original lateral-shuffle previews show rope waves with a wide travelling stance. The current Muscle & Strength alternating-wave reference does not establish side travel. Continuous waves during actual lateral displacement and the new publisher’s professional provenance remain to be established together. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Medicine Ball Slam
entries.editorialNote: Steph Gaudreau public previews show standing with a ball raised overhead followed by a downward floor slam. This establishes the ball and downward throw rather than an unweighted movement. Ball construction and rebound remain equipment-specific; no automatic rebound catch is adopted.

entries.name: Rotational Medicine Ball Slam
entries.editorialNote: JS FIT’s original description specifies raising the ball overhead and slamming to one side; its previews show the low side finish. The current Muscle & Strength comparison slams centrally. Onnit’s article separately discusses rotational slams. The outside-foot placement and a sufficiently attributed exact video remain unresolved. A central slam does not establish the rotational finish. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Medicine Ball Rotational Scoop Toss
entries.editorialNote: Simone Sports Performance’s candidate previews show standing rotational medicine-ball work at a wall, unlike Victor Lopez’s explicitly half-kneeling video and the existing kneeling comparator. Need to establish the low scoop release, back-hip loading and standing side-on sequence in the closer source; standing chest passes must remain distinct. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Medicine Ball Shot Put Throw
entries.editorialNote: Muscle & Strength original Rotational Medicine Ball Shot Put preview shows a standing side-on stance with the ball near one shoulder and the single-arm shot-put setup. The complete hip/foot pivot, release and wall rebound still require motion review; no rebound behaviour is assumed.

entries.name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
entries.editorialNote: Human Kinetics chest-pass reference; compare stance, partner/wall target and catching arrangement.

entries.name: Medicine Ball Overhead Wall Throw
entries.editorialNote: NeuStrength describes a medicine ball lifted overhead for a wall throw and its previews show an overhead stance facing a wall. The existing Physitrack overhead-toss label does not establish the required step-in wall-directed sequence. The step-in soccer-throw action, wall target and the new publisher’s professional basis remain unresolved together. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Medicine Ball Vertical Toss
entries.editorialNote: Michael Jeanfavre and Billyduke Physio supply named vertical-toss candidates; public previews show a ball lifted overhead. This is closer in direction than the generic overhead toss. The catalog requires a squat, jump, vertical release and allowing the ball to bounce. The preview evidence does not establish all four phases or the exit. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Medicine Ball Russian Twist
entries.editorialNote: Red Dot Fitness’s original medicine-ball Russian-twist previews show seated floor support, a medicine ball held in both hands and rotation beside the hips. The primary staff page documents a professional strength-coaching and athletic-training team. The catalog medicine-ball load is supported; grounded versus lifted feet and the individual rotation range remain variants. Team qualifications are not attributed to the unnamed model. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Medicine Ball V-Up
entries.editorialNote: LivestrongWoman’s medicine-ball V-up previews keep the ball in the hands as the torso and legs rise. Exercise Library’s similarly named candidate also does not establish a transfer between hands and feet. The catalog specifically passes the ball from hands to feet. A weighted V-up without a transfer remains related, regardless of the shared name. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Medicine Ball Push-Up
entries.editorialNote: Named exercise reference; compare the linked source setup with the internal technique notes.

entries.name: Medicine Ball Lunge with Rotation
entries.editorialNote: Nicole Dudas and Shuichi Take show medicine-ball lunge/rotation candidates in their previews. The current PureGym reference is a reverse lunge without the medicine-ball turn. Need a forward lunge with rotation over the front knee and documented professional provenance for the selected exact clip; reverse-lunge and opposite-direction turns remain different. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Medicine Ball Woodchop
entries.editorialNote: WeStrive’s original clip credits featured trainer David Miguens and identifies its library as trainer-made. Its public previews show a held medicine ball travelling on a diagonal between a high shoulder position and the opposite low side, rather than a cable or released throw. This is a professional coaching-software publisher’s attribution, not independent verification of the featured trainer’s current certification. Complete motion and foot pivot remain unreviewed. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: BOSU Squat
entries.editorialNote: Rehab My Patient public previews show a squat while standing on the rounded dome with the flat base on the floor. This resolves the BOSU support and orientation. Full video motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: BOSU Push-Up
entries.editorialNote: BOSU push-up reference; confirm which surface faces the floor.

entries.name: BOSU Mountain Climber
entries.editorialNote: Official BOSU clip previews show hands holding the platform edges with the dome on the floor and alternating knees drawn forward from a high plank. This replaces the floor hold comparison. Full video motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: BOSU Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
entries.editorialNote: Totus Fitness explicitly identifies its candidate as flat-side-down, and previews show a single-leg hinge standing on the dome. Elite Wellness’s other candidate shows a different balance-surface arrangement. The dome-up hinge is a promising closer match, but the creator’s professional provenance and complete support/control remain unresolved. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: BOSU Lateral Step-Over
entries.editorialNote: Be Fitness Training’s original description specifies stepping laterally over a BOSU and its previews show the dome-supported transfer. Ames Elite has a similar named candidate. The current Rehab Hero comparison is a lateral step-up. Need a sufficiently established professional original publisher and complete side-to-side over-dome sequence; stepping onto a rigid box alone is insufficient. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: BOSU Reverse Lunge
entries.editorialNote: The official BOSU reverse-lunge previews keep the rear foot on the dome. Fredericksburg Fitness’s closer candidate appears to put the front foot on the dome while the other leg moves back. The catalog front-foot-on-dome arrangement differs from the official clip. The closer candidate’s professional basis and exact stepping sequence remain unresolved. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: BOSU Side Plank
entries.editorialNote: QuickCoach’s original instructions explicitly place a forearm on the dome with the flat base on the floor, stack the feet and hold a raised side plank. The inspected public previews show that support arrangement. A professional coaching-software reference supports setup identity, not an individual medical credential, a suitable hold duration or approval of continuous execution. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: BOSU Squat Jump
entries.editorialNote: BOSU’s official Pulse Squat Jump begins and continues on top of the balance trainer. Nicole Murphy’s candidate previews also show the exerciser already on the dome. The catalog starts on the floor, jumps onto the dome and steps down. An on-dome jump sequence is not an exact entry/exit reference. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Monkey Bar Traverse
entries.editorialNote: The NASM original pull-up description fixes both hands on a single bar and raises/lowers the torso. It does not describe releasing one hand and progressing to the next rung. A credible rung-to-rung traverse demonstration remains missing; a pull-up or dead hang validates neither travel nor hand-release sequencing. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Toes-to-Bar
entries.editorialNote: Jacob Goodin’s original toes-to-bar description explicitly identifies a hanging bar setup, raising the toes to the bar and limiting swing. Public previews show the hanging raised-leg implementation. This replaces the less specific hanging-leg-raise comparison. The anti-swing instruction supports the intended controlled variant; repeated toe contact and all repetitions have not been inspected. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Hanging Windshield Wiper
entries.editorialNote: Scott Herman’s specifically named hanging-windshield-wiper video and inspected previews establish a hanging raised-leg implementation. The catalog says to sweep raised legs side to side and does not require bent knees. The video is the advanced straight-leg configuration. The internal notes deliberately begin with bent knees and a small arc; that regression is not presented as the filmed variant. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Commando Pull-Up
entries.editorialNote: Live Lean’s original description explicitly identifies a hands-together front/back grip and alternating head positions; BecomingBamboo has another original commando candidate. These are closer than the bilateral NASM pull-up. The new creators’ professional publishing basis remains insufficiently established here; the front/back grip and alternate-side sequence need an accepted exact source. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Archer Pull-Up
entries.editorialNote: Pullup & Dip’s original tutorial separates typewriter, ring, band-assisted and unassisted archer phases. Player positions at 0:46, 0:51, 1:01 and 1:06 were inspected; some contain overlays or different progressions. The complete unassisted bar archer repetition with the other arm straight is not established by the selected positions. Do not treat ring or assisted phases as the target. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Plate Front Raise
entries.editorialNote: Rehab My Patient public previews show one plate held with two hands in front and raised forward while standing. This replaces the dumbbell front-raise comparison. Full video motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Plate Halo
entries.editorialNote: OriGym public previews show one weight plate held at its edges with two hands and passed around the head. This resolves the plate-versus-kettlebell implement difference. Full video motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Plate Pinch Carry
entries.editorialNote: Steph Gaudreau public previews show walking with weight plates held by a fingertip pinch at the sides. This distinguishes the grip from a dumbbell farmer carry. Full video motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Plate Russian Twist
entries.editorialNote: Live Lean’s plate-twist description names a plate and its previews show one held during seated rotation, but the prose mistakenly calls it a medicine ball in one step. Black Lion has another plate-specific candidate. Professional provenance for the closer original clip remains unverified here; keep the plate/medicine-ball wording conflict explicit rather than copying it. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Turkish Get-Up
entries.editorialNote: Named exercise reference; compare the linked source setup with the internal technique notes.

entries.name: Kettlebell Clean and Press
entries.editorialNote: Mark Wildman has an original clean-and-press primer, but the inspected preview stills show explanation rather than the complete combination. Nuffield’s named clean-and-press page is gated. The existing StrongFirst video covers the military press. The clean into rack and subsequent overhead press must be established together in accessible original footage. A press-only clip does not cover the clean. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Kettlebell Snatch
entries.editorialNote: StrongFirst snatch-path instruction selected, distinct from a two-handed swing.

entries.name: Smith Machine Hip Thrust
entries.editorialNote: NeuStrength’s original description and previews show upper-back bench support with a Smith bar over the hips; Keren Zumba has a similar setup tutorial. PureGym’s current video instead uses a free barbell. The closer Smith candidate needs a stronger professional provenance and verification of padding, safety stops and rail-specific setup; free-bar support is not equivalent. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Dumbbell Glute Bridge

Its embedded Vimeo ID was discovered, but provider metadata were redacted and standalone access was unavailable. Other previews show EZ bars without an established professional basis. An accessible, individually identified original EZ-bar demonstration remains unresolved. The existing straight-bar curl is retained as a comparison. entries.name: Assisted Pull-Up Machine

entries.name: Assisted Dip Machine
entries.editorialNote: DVIDS has a specifically titled assisted-dip machine feature, but the inspected samples mainly show equipment and the presenter. Fitness Lab’s previews show an assisted station, without firmly establishing the catalog kneeling-pad arrangement. Need the knee-pad counterweight support during the actual dip. An ordinary dip and a standing foot-platform model are not silently equated. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Sled Push
entries.editorialNote: Named exercise reference; compare the linked source setup with the internal technique notes.

entries.name: Sled Pull
entries.editorialNote: Rogue's original equipment demonstration identifies both forward and backward sled drags. Public previews show Matt Chan holding straps in front while moving backward, matching the catalog strap-drag version. Only the backward hand-held strap segment matches. A harness drag and a stationary hand-over-hand pull remain separate variants.

entries.name: Sandbag Bear-Hug Carry
entries.editorialNote: Named exercise reference; compare the linked source setup with the internal technique notes.

entries.name: Sandbag Squat
entries.editorialNote: UTSA Campus Recreation’s original sandbag-squat previews hold a handled bag in front of the shoulders. OPEX’s original description puts the bag across the traps. Neither shows the catalog arms-wrapped bear hug at the chest. A true bear-hug sandbag squat remains unresolved. Handle-held front-rack and shoulder-loaded positions are distinct. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
entries.editorialNote: PureGym explicitly describes kneeling, holding an ab wheel, rolling forward while controlling the trunk and rolling back. This establishes the kneeling ab-wheel configuration. Full video motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Ankle-Weight Glute Kickback
entries.editorialNote: Kiana Loomis’s original candidate previews show quadruped support and an ankle weight during a rear leg lift. Hart Athletics instead shows a standing weighted kickback. PureGym’s current donkey-kick comparison is unloaded. The quadruped candidate is closer, but its original professional provenance and the hip-extension path remain unverified together. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Ankle-Weight Side-Lying Leg Raise
entries.editorialNote: The current Physitrack side-lying hip-abduction reference establishes side support and a top-leg raise, but the linked reference set does not establish an ankle cuff weight. Need visible ankle-weight loading and controlled top-leg abduction; bodyweight technique alone does not verify the loaded variant. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Back Extension
entries.editorialNote: Physitrack instructions and sampled frames show ankles secured on a back-extension bench, the hip pad at the upper thighs and hinging over that pad to a straight body line. This replaces the prone floor extension comparator. Full video motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: A-skips
entries.editorialNote: Named clinician-library skipping reference. Full running-drill rhythm has not been visually reviewed.

entries.name: Arm circles
entries.editorialNote: Marine Corps Force Fitness sampled frames show standing with both arms extended to the sides and changing arm-circle positions. The dedicated demonstration establishes the standing arm-circle configuration. Full video motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Band dislocates
entries.editorialNote: Stick Mobility’s original resistance-band dislocate/passthrough demonstration and previews show a wide two-hand band grip passing overhead to behind the body. Its own manufacturer/education page documents the movement-training publishing context. Only the comfortable passthrough phase is relevant. Extra band-wrapping phases, forced end range and broad benefit claims are not adopted. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Band pull-aparts
entries.editorialNote: Rogue manufacturer public previews show a light elastic band held at chest/shoulder height and the hands spreading apart horizontally toward the chest. This establishes the band pull-apart configuration. Full video motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Banded lateral walks
entries.editorialNote: NASM lateral band walk; band around ankles in the description. Compare with any above-knee placement.

entries.name: Lateral band walks
entries.editorialNote: NASM lateral band walk; band around ankles in the description. Compare with any above-knee placement.

entries.name: Bodyweight squats to a bench
entries.editorialNote: The Physitrack sit-to-stand reference uses a seat; the internal guide permits a controlled touch or supported seated start on a bench. That is closer than the earlier blanket distinction between all sit-to-stands and bench squats. The sampled reference still does not establish the specific stable bench and chosen contact strategy. Keep the chair/bench and touch-versus-seated-start differences visible. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Broad jumps
entries.editorialNote: Named exercise reference; compare the linked source setup with the internal technique notes.

entries.name: Broomstick or towel pass-throughs
entries.editorialNote: Dowel pass-through reference; band/towel implementation is a related implement adaptation.

entries.name: Cat-cow
entries.editorialNote: Named exercise reference; compare the linked source setup with the internal technique notes.

entries.name: Dead hang
entries.editorialNote: Physitrack instructions specify an overhead bar, straight arms, feet clear of the floor and a timed hanging position; sampled frames show this support configuration. The source adds buttock tension; the guide permits a comfortable dead hang and does not prescribe a universally passive or active shoulder position.

entries.name: Downward dog to plank
entries.editorialNote: Physitrack's prone-push-up-to-downward-dog instructions explicitly pass through a straight-arm plank, push the hips up/back and reverse the transition. Sampled frames show that floor-supported inverted-V phase. Only its plank-to-downward-dog transition matches this guide. The separate push-up phase is not added to the guide repetition.

entries.name: Explosive push-ups
entries.editorialNote: Plyometric push-up reference.

entries.name: Fast bodyweight squats
entries.editorialNote: The current Physitrack bodyweight-squat reference supports an unloaded bilateral squat, but no brisk repetition cadence was established in this pass. The guide’s fast-but-controlled pace remains unverified. A standard squat reference does not independently validate faster execution or suitability for an interval. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Fast incline push-ups
entries.editorialNote: PureGym’s incline-push-up source establishes raised-hand pressing, but not the guide’s brisk cadence. The guide does not require an airborne plyometric push-up. Need a controlled fast incline press demonstration; do not invent a flight requirement or use an ordinary cadence as evidence for the faster one. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Glute bridges
entries.editorialNote: Named exercise reference; compare the linked source setup with the internal technique notes.

entries.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch with reach
entries.editorialNote: Steady State Health’s original description adds the same-side overhead reach to a half-kneeling hip-flexor stretch, and its previews show that reach. It also adds a side lean. A stronger documented professional basis and a clear distinction between the catalog reach and the optional added side bend remain needed. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: High-knee marches
entries.editorialNote: Rehab Hero describes alternating a knee and the opposite arm to roughly hip/shoulder height from standing. Public previews show the in-place A-march with opposite arm coordination. This fills the high-knee-march video gap. The running-drill name A March is a naming equivalence; no running or skipping phase is implied.

entries.name: Hip circles
entries.editorialNote: Queensland instructions specify standing with hands on hips and circling the pelvis in both directions; sampled frames show that standing setup. This replaces quadruped hip circles. Full video motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Hug-yourself twists
entries.editorialNote: Queensland instructions and sampled frames show standing with folded arms and turning the upper torso left/right. This replaces the seated trunk-rotation comparison. Full video motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Inchworms
entries.editorialNote: Named inchworm reference.

entries.name: Incline push-ups on a bench
entries.editorialNote: Eric Foxman’s original incline-push-up-on-bench video and previews show both hands supported on a stable bench and feet on the floor. His primary biography states ACE personal-training certification and a longstanding training practice. Bench support is established, replacing the generic incline comparison. The amount of incline and complete repetitions remain unreviewed; certification renewal was not checked. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Incline push-ups
entries.editorialNote: Named exercise reference; compare the linked source setup with the internal technique notes.

entries.name: Lat stretch holding a post
entries.editorialNote: NASM’s current original lat-stretch instructions use kneeling support with a forearm on a ball. Rehab Hero’s lat-stretch-row instead uses a resistance band and adds rowing. The target is a standing hip hinge while holding a post. Neither a ball-supported stretch nor an active band row establishes that support/action combination. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Lateral shuffles
entries.editorialNote: Special Olympics labels the drill Side Shuffles; public previews show a standing athletic stance with sideways steps and uncrossed legs. This establishes the lateral shuffle rather than an unspecified change-of-direction drill. Full video motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Leg swings, front to back and side to side
entries.editorialNote: Special Olympics publishes a combined forward and lateral leg-swing demonstration. Public previews show a standing person using a chair for support and swinging the free leg in the two named directions. The updated combined clip is selected. Full sequencing, cadence and comfortable range still need playback review.

entries.name: Leg swings, front to back
entries.editorialNote: Special Olympics combined leg-swing demonstration includes the supported front-to-back component; public previews show the chair-supported forward swing. Only its forward-swing section is relevant here; the separate lateral component is not part of this guide repetition.

entries.name: Low box jumps
entries.editorialNote: PureGym box-jump previews show a low box in front of the athlete and a two-foot reception onto its top. This establishes the forward low-box task rather than lateral or single-leg jumping. Full landing mechanics and deliberate step-down behaviour remain unreviewed in motion.

entries.name: Marching knee lifts
entries.editorialNote: Queensland written instructions and sampled frames show standing alternating knee lifts with coordinated opposite arm movement. This supplies a direct full-video reference rather than a GIF alone. Full video motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Medicine ball chest pass
entries.editorialNote: Human Kinetics chest-pass reference; compare stance, partner/wall target and catching arrangement.

entries.name: Open books lying on your side
entries.editorialNote: Side-lying version selected. Rehab Hero also has a standing split-stance drill with the same open-book title.

entries.name: Thoracic open books
entries.editorialNote: Side-lying version selected. Rehab Hero also has a standing split-stance drill with the same open-book title.

entries.name: Prone Y-T-W raises
entries.editorialNote: Physitrack’s prone series includes extension, T, Y and an explicitly named L with additional forearm rotation. The ITPA workbook separately describes the requested Y-T-W shapes on a bench or ball. An inspected floor/bench Y-T-W video with a true W remains missing. Do not count L or additional rotation phases as a literal W sequence. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Push-up to downward dog
entries.editorialNote: Physitrack instructions describe pressing from prone into a straight-arm plank and then pushing back to downward dog; sampled frames show the floor support and raised-hip phase. The complete transition timing and spinal control remain unreviewed in motion.

entries.name: Push-ups
entries.editorialNote: Named exercise reference; compare the linked source setup with the internal technique notes.

entries.name: Reach-and-pull
entries.editorialNote: The current Physitrack comparison is a seated machine row. The guide asks for unloaded arms reaching overhead and elbows then pulling down beside the ribs. A search result mentioned the phrase within a longer warm-up without an inspected original segment. Unloaded overhead reach-to-pull sequence remains unresolved; a resisted horizontal row is not the same direction or support. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Reverse arm swings
entries.editorialNote: The current reference performs shoulder circles. The guide specifies bilateral forward/backward arm swings, which do not require a complete circular path. Need the intended forward/back swing action from a credible original demonstration, rather than relabelling circumduction. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Reverse lunges in place
entries.editorialNote: PureGym’s original reverse-lunge description establishes stepping backward and returning, but allows loading and does not itself prove the unloaded guide implementation. Confirm an unloaded in-place reverse-lunge demonstration; the catalog’s loaded reverse-lunge variants are not automatically valid for the bodyweight warm-up. Full continuous motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Scap pull-ups
entries.editorialNote: Written section confirms straight-elbow scapular depression from a dead hang.

entries.name: Scap push-ups
entries.editorialNote: Queensland explicitly demonstrates elevated scapular push-ups and permits lowering the support to the floor. The internal guide also permits a stable incline, so this is an allowed support configuration. This does not mean the desk clip is direct evidence of floor execution.

entries.name: Side lunges
entries.editorialNote: Named exercise reference; compare the linked source setup with the internal technique notes.

entries.name: Bodyweight good mornings
entries.editorialNote: Horton Barbell public previews show standing with no external load, hands beside the head and a hip hinge to/from a forward torso angle. This resolves the loaded-barbell comparison. Full video motion and professional technique approval remain unreviewed.

entries.name: Calf raises
entries.editorialNote: Named exercise reference; compare the linked source setup with the internal technique notes.

entries.name: Deep squat hold
entries.editorialNote: Jayd Harrison and SHRP have deep-squat-hold candidates whose public previews show a low held squat. The existing Rehab Hero clip adds repeated torso rotations. Physitrack’s weighted deep-squat page adds a plate. An ordinary held squat allows support or a counterbalance in the guide, but heel contact, hold rather than repeated movement, and publisher provenance for the new candidates remain unresolved together.
